data.why: The repo bundles curated positive/negative controls in assets/examples that the app's own 'Load selected control' buttons and file-uploader already expect in FASTA form, so these are handed to the browser as upload candidates instead of inventing data.

goals: Load a known positive-control locus (MIR21) and confirm it ranks highly with a clear explainable evidence trail
Paste or upload an arbitrary DNA/RNA sequence and get a ranked shortlist of candidate pre-miRNA hairpins
Fetch an hg38 genomic locus by chromosome and coordinates and fold it to look for precursor candidates
Inspect a single candidate's secondary structure, folding energy, and feature-influence breakdown to judge why it ranked where it did
Compare a positive control against a negative/Rfam-decoy control side by side to see which evidence layers separate true precursors from look-alikes
Review the held-out benchmark metrics and stress tests to calibrate trust in the classifier before taking a candidate to the lab

review.summary: The tree states the README's purpose exactly (rank pre-miRNA-like hairpins with independent evidence, for triage before lab work, not discovery). Its four phases and 14 tasks are at the right depth and well backed by evidence that the second agent replayed in full. It needs only small fixes before filing: one mis-cited paste screen, the effect of protein-region masking, and the per-candidate 'Evidence this analysis does not provide' panel.
